text: The problem is having to operate a slide deck while explaining something.
A presenter is distracted by searching for the next page in a rigid slide sequence.
We move through capture, understanding, matching, and visual composition.
These four stages connect sound from the microphone to the final explanation.
The matcher checks similarity and the gap between the top two topics.
When the system is unsure which concept was meant it holds its current focus.
A fixed slide deck and a flexible canvas organize a presentation differently.
With slides the order is fixed; with this canvas you can revisit ideas in any order.
We separate cloud preparation before the talk from local browser inference during it.
Whisper and the embedding model run on the device rather than sending live speech to a server.
My final takeaway is that ideas should set the pace of the presentation.
To conclude, the speaker can focus on explaining naturally with manual control available.
